_formula.name: Hutash Score

benchmark.description: Published benchmark score, normalized to 0-10 via min-max scaling within a realistic floor/ceiling for the modality (not simple division)
benchmark.bounds_note: Bounds are set at realistic floor/ceiling for the modality, not based on current best model. Scores remain stable when new models are added.

popularity.method: 10 × log10(downloads+1) / log10(baseline_downloads+1), where baseline is the most-downloaded model in the same modality (translation: google-t5/t5-small, 22.9M downloads). Log scale, not linear — raw download counts span several orders of magnitude across models, so a linear ratio would crush nearly everything to ~0.

_formula.future: v1.1 will add user ratings (50% weight, benchmark 35%, popularity 15%)

Popularity added for the first time (previously untracked): normalized against a live-verified HF pipeline-tag ranking, not a guess.

benchmark.source: ACE-Step 1.5 technical report — outperforms Suno v5

popularity.baseline: facebook/musicgen-medium (1.96M downloads) — #1 HF text-to-audio model, used as the music-modality baseline

ace-step-1.5.note: Recalculated under the new min-max normalization (METHODOLOGY.md, 2026-08-17): benchmark 8.7→8.375. Popularity added for the first time and is a genuine data-completeness caveat, not a formula artifact: the HuggingFace API's own 'downloads' field for ACE-Step/ACE-Step-v1-3.5B returns 0 despite 744 likes, most likely because this repo's weights aren't distributed through the standard tracked-download path — this pulls the overall score down sharply (5.86) even though the underlying model quality (SongEval 4.35, a strong result per its own technical report) is unchanged. Flagging rather than substituting a guessed number; revisit if HuggingFace's download tracking for this repo changes.

qwen3-1.7b.note: Qwen3 1.7B (Q8_0 GGUF, CPU-only) — general-purpose LLM, no longer an internal-only tool. Scores are engineering estimates from the model's specs (1.7B parameters, INT8 quantization, CPU inference via llama.cpp) rather than a formal benchmark run — replace with real numbers if Qwen publishes official MMLU/benchmark results for this checkpoint. 2026-08-17 min-max normalization update (METHODOLOGY.md) reviewed: no change to this entry — there is still no real benchmark number to normalize, so the new min-max formula has nothing to apply to.

gemma4-e4b.note: Gemma 4 E4B (GGUF, native tool calling) — general-purpose ~4B-effective-parameter LLM. Live web research (Aug 2026) could not produce a benchmark number reliable enough to cite: two sources gave conflicting MMLU-Pro figures for this checkpoint (69.4% per the huggingface.co/google/gemma-4-E4B-it model card vs. 77.2% per third-party blog aggregation), and a fetched arXiv 'technical report' in the same research pass misattributed Gemma to an unrelated company entirely instead of its real publisher, Google DeepMind — a clear fabrication that undermines confidence in the rest of that source. hutash_score is an engineering estimate only (newer model generation and larger effective parameter count than qwen3-1.7b, same reasoning as that entry's own estimate) — replace with a real number once Google's own official benchmark table can be verified against a primary source. 2026-08-17 min-max normalization update (METHODOLOGY.md) reviewed: no change to this entry — there is still no real benchmark number to normalize, so the new min-max formula has nothing to apply to.

qwen3.5-4b.note: Qwen3.5 4B (GGUF, native tool calling) — general-purpose 4B parameter LLM. Live web research (Aug 2026) surfaced an MMLU-Pro figure of 79.1% from a fetched huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3.5-4B model card — unusually high for a 4B model and gathered in the same research pass that produced a confirmed fabrication for the companion gemma4-e4b entry (see its note), so it is not cited here without independent confirmation. hutash_score is an engineering estimate only (newer model generation and larger parameter count than qwen3-1.7b, same reasoning as that entry's own estimate) — replace with a real number once Alibaba's own official benchmark table can be verified against a primary source. 2026-08-17 min-max normalization update (METHODOLOGY.md) reviewed: no change to this entry — there is still no real benchmark number to normalize, so the new min-max formula has nothing to apply to.

indicconformer-600m.note: IndicConformer 600M (AI4Bharat, hybrid CTC/RNNT, 22 Indian languages) — engineering estimate, not a formal benchmark run. Scored relative to this catalogue's existing STT entries (whisper-large-v3 9.7, distil-whisper-large-v3 9.6, whisper-tiny 9.4 — all scored against English-centric WER benchmarks that don't cover Indian-language accuracy at all) rather than against those numbers directly: AI4Bharat's own IndicConformer technical reports claim competitive WER against Whisper on Indian-language test sets specifically, but no single normalized-scale (0-10, WER-derived) figure comparable to the Whisper entries' own methodology could be sourced and verified live for this exact 600M checkpoint. Replace with a real WER-normalized score once AI4Bharat publishes (or this checkpoint is benchmarked against) a directly comparable Indian-language test set figure. 2026-08-17 min-max normalization update (METHODOLOGY.md) reviewed: no change to this entry — there is still no real benchmark number to normalize, so the new min-max formula has nothing to apply to.

indic-parler-tts.note: Indic Parler-TTS (AI4Bharat fine-tune of Parler-TTS, 17 Indian languages + English) — engineering estimate, not a formal benchmark run. Scored just below parler-tts-mini-1.1 (7.6, itself a UTMOS-based community-consensus estimate, not a raw model benchmark) on the reasoning that a multilingual fine-tune spread across 18 languages typically trades a little per-language quality for breadth relative to the English-only base checkpoint it derives from, absent a directly comparable UTMOS figure for the Indic-language checkpoint itself. Replace with a real benchmark score once a UTMOS or equivalent MOS figure specific to this checkpoint's Indian-language output can be sourced and verified. 2026-08-17 min-max normalization update (METHODOLOGY.md) reviewed: no change to this entry — there is still no real benchmark number to normalize, so the new min-max formula has nothing to apply to.

indictrans2-1b.note: IndicTrans2 1B (AI4Bharat, English ↔ 22 Indian languages) — engineering estimate, not a formal benchmark run. AI4Bharat's own published BLEU/chrF++ figures on the IN22-Gen/IN22-Conv benchmarks describe the full IndicTrans2 model family, not isolated to this exact 1B En-Indic checkpoint, and are not on the 0-10 normalized scale the rest of this catalogue uses, so no single comparable number could be sourced and verified live. Scored as the catalogue's first dedicated translation model — first-party AI4Bharat research release, purpose-built and evaluated specifically for Indian-language translation (unlike MADLAD-400's broad 400+-language generalist scope) — rather than against any of the STT/TTS entries' own unrelated metrics. Replace with a real normalized score once a directly comparable IN22 figure for this specific checkpoint can be verified against a primary source. 2026-08-17 min-max normalization update (METHODOLOGY.md) reviewed: no change to this entry — there is still no real benchmark number to normalize, so the new min-max formula has nothing to apply to.

benchmark.source: MADLAD-400 paper (Kudugunta et al.), Table 4, MT-3B model, WMT en2xx direction

popularity.baseline: google-t5/t5-small (22.9M downloads) — most-downloaded translation-pipeline model on HuggingFace

madlad400-3b.note: Recalculated under the new min-max normalization (METHODOLOGY.md, 2026-08-17): benchmark 2.82→5.16 (BLEU's new 5-50 floor/ceiling reflects that 28.2 BLEU is genuinely strong MT quality, unlike the old /10 division which flattened it near the bottom of the scale). Popularity re-verified live against the HuggingFace API: downloads/likes have grown to 229,192/216 (from the ~50K/120 figures given in the original task brief, which were explicitly flagged there as unverified) — using the current, verified numbers rather than the stale estimate.

opus-mt-en-hi.note: Helsinki-NLP opus-mt-en-hi (MarianMT, English to Hindi) — engineering estimate, not a formal benchmark run. Scored as a lightweight CPU translation model: small, fast and dependency-light enough to run comfortably without a GPU, and good for basic translation, but less accurate than MADLAD-400. No comparable normalized figure was sourced: the model card's BLEU numbers are per-testset (newsdev/newstest) rather than the single normalized value the rest of this catalogue carries, and none was verified live, so `benchmark` stays null rather than holding a number nobody checked. ORDERING CAVEAT, recorded rather than smoothed over: this 6.0 sits ABOVE madlad400-3b's 5.79, which reads oddly next to the accuracy comparison above. madlad's score is formula-derived and pulled down by the min-max BLEU normalization (28.2 BLEU -> 5.16 benchmark), while this one is an estimate on the same 0-10 scale but not through the same pipeline — the two are not strictly comparable, and indictrans2-1b's 8.6 is an estimate of the same kind. Replace with a real normalized score once a directly comparable BLEU figure for this checkpoint can be verified against a primary source.

popularity.baseline: hexgrad/Kokoro-82M (12.4M downloads) — #1 HF text-to-speech model; updated from the previous t5-small/translation placeholder now that a real TTS baseline has been established (used consistently for kokoro/parler-tts-mini-1.1/svara-tts)

svara-tts.note: Svara-TTS v1 (Kenpath Technologies, 19 Indian languages + Indian English, Orpheus/Llama-3.2-3B-based) — engineering estimate for the benchmark/quality component, not a formula-calculated hutash_score: live research (Aug 2026) found no published MOS, UTMOS, or other quality-metric score for this checkpoint anywhere — not on the model card, not in the inference repo, not in third-party coverage — so the formula's 70%-weighted benchmark component has no real input to calculate from. Scored via the same engineering-estimate pattern already used for indicconformer-600m/indic-parler-tts/indictrans2-1b/madlad400-3b's prior placeholder: positioned near chatterbox (8.43) and above dia-1.6b (7.15) and parler-tts-mini-1.1 (6.21), reflecting real, verified popularity (234,058 downloads/month, 53 likes per the HuggingFace API — notably higher traction than this catalogue's other recent Indic-language additions) plus the widest per-model language coverage in this catalogue (19 languages) and an ungated, Apache-2.0, actively-maintained release. The task brief cited '800K+ downloads' (Kenpath's own claim, presumably all-time cumulative); the HuggingFace API's own 'downloads' field returns 234,058 (a rolling/monthly figure, the same metric basis used for every other popularity number in this file) — used the verified API figure for the popularity calculation rather than the unverifiable cumulative claim, and note both here for transparency. Replace hutash_score with a formula-calculated one once a verified MOS/UTMOS figure for this checkpoint can be sourced. 2026-08-17 min-max normalization update (METHODOLOGY.md) reviewed: doesn't change this entry's hutash_score since benchmark is still null — only the popularity baseline was refreshed (now kokoro, a real TTS-modality reference, instead of the old translation-modality placeholder). Replace hutash_score with a formula-calculated one once a verified MOS/UTMOS figure for this checkpoint can be sourced.
